h.select_rule: Keep hypotheses you rate at least 55% likely true but expect other models to rate below 50%, and name the specific naive reasoning that would mislead them. Drop anything you rate below 50% yourself, and anything obvious from structure alone. Keep fields and directions diverse.
h.strategy: Propose a broad, varied set of conditional hypotheses covering many different edited fields, conditioning fields and both directions. For each, briefly note your own probability that it holds and how an intuitive reader would judge it.

hyps.why: Replacing none with a conv adds a whole learnable path, which gains far more than swapping one existing op for another.
Replacing none with a conv on the input edge activates node 1, which gains more than replacing an op that already works.
Replacing a strong conv with a pool loses accuracy, unlike replacing a weak op.
Downgrading a conv to a pool hurts more than changing a weak op.
Output inputs are redundant when edge 5 is already a strong conv.
Without the direct edge, a strong conv on edge 4 is a main route to the output.
A skip on edge 3 already gives a good path to the output, so edge 5 matters less.
A strong conv on edge 5 already supplies the output, so a skip adds less.
Adding a conv where there was no edge gains more than swapping one op for another.
With edge 0 none, edge 3 is the main route from the input to the output.
